title: AffrescoUI App
description: An app's manifest, app.json in the app's folder: what a stock host needs to run it. Read by Screen::fromApp(), the host and `affrescoui check`. Specification: SCREEN_FORMAT.md, "Apps: app.json".

id.description: The app's id: the person's data and decisions are kept by it, in <data folder>/apps/<id>.

name.description: Its name, shown by the host.

icon.description: Its icon: an image in its folder.

themes.description: Its own kits and themes: files of components, styles, tokens, colors and fonts, merged into the entry screen after its own includes (the screen's entries win).

capabilities.description: What it asks the person for. Nothing is allowed until the person allows it, for this app only; a revision of the screen never uses more than these.

network.description: Origins its connections reach, each with why: "https://api.example.com", or "https://*.example.com" for its subdomains. http and ws reach the computer's own (loopback) addresses only.

folders.description: Folders its services read or write, by the root name they use ("workspace"): the person picks the folder.

programs.description: Programs its process services run: a name on the PATH, "shell" or "git".

audio.description: Sound on the system's output (the screen's audio section).

assistant.description: The host's own agent, which answers the screen's ask steps with the provider of intelligence the person set up.

files.description: The open and save dialogs: saveFile, openFile, export, and an image step's open and save.

windows.description: The screen's other windows (its windows section, opened by openWindow).

channels.description: The screen's channels: programs it talks to over sockets in its own host's socket folder, or peers at a wss:// address.

models.description: A file of data models and queries, merged into the entry screen.

seed.description: A collection's first records, imported on first run: a JSON list of records, or a CSV file whose header names the fields (an "id" column gives the ids).

assets.description: Its other files and folders (images, sounds, fonts), shipped with it.

why.description: What the app does with it, shown to the person when it asks.

path.description: A file or folder inside the app's folder: relative, no ".." part, '/' between parts.
